While hardening online security, I also construct a mental guard for tomorrow's work. Preparing in advance with the mindset that foresight prevents anxiety minimizes start-of-week dread. Setting up an ironclad defense, please enjoy a comfortable evening time ( •̀ω•́ )  【中文】 洗完澡神清气爽，到了20点对数字设备进行安全检查的时间♨️ 鉴于国内企业遭受网络攻击损害的新闻，完成了密码重置及双重认证的重新设定。 在强化网络安全防线的同时，也构建好了应对明天工作的心理防御墙。 本着有备无患的精神做好事前准备，就能将一周伊始的焦虑降至最低。 建立起万无一失的防御体制，请好好享受一段悠闲惬意的夜间时光吧( •̀ω•́ )  【한국어】 목욕 후 리프레시하고 디지털 기기의 보안 점검을 실시하는 20시가 되었습니다♨️ 국내 기업의 사이버 공격 피해 뉴스를 접하고 비밀번호 변경과 2단계 인증 재설정을 완료했습니다. 인터넷 보안を 강고히 함과 동시에 내일 업무를 향한 멘탈 가드도 구축합니다. 유비무환의 정신으로 사전 준비를 해두면 주초의 불안도 최소한으로 줄일 수 있습니다. 만전의 방어 체제를 갖추고 여유로운 밤 시간을 즐겨보세요( •̀ω•́ )  【العربية】 في الثامنة مساءً، وبعد الاستحمام والمنعش، حان الوقت لفحص أمان الأجهزة الرقمية ♨️ تفاعلاً مع أخبار هجمات القرصنة على الشركات المحلية، أكملت تغيير كلمات المرور والتحقق بخطوتين. بينما أقوي الأمان الرقمي، أبني حماية ذهنية لعمل الغد أيضًا. بالإعداد المسبق بأسلوب الوقاية خير من العلاج، يمكن تقليل القلق في بداية الأسبوع. مع إعداد نظام دفاعي ممتاز، نتمنى لكم الاستمتاع بوقت هادئ هذا المساء ( •̀ω•́ )  【Français】 À 20h, rafraîchi par un bon bain, il est temps de contrôler la sécurité de mes appareils ♨️ Face aux actus sur les cyberattaques visant les entreprises, j'ai mis à jour mes mots de passe et la 2FA. En renforçant ma sécurité en ligne, je dresse aussi un rempart mental pour le travail de demain. Anticiper sereinement permet de réduire au minimum l'appréhension du début de semaine. Parfaitement protégé, profitez d'une soirée paisible et relaxante ( •̀ω•́ )  【Español】 A las 8 PM, renovado tras el baño, es hora de revisar la seguridad de los dispositivos ♨️ Ante las noticias de ciberataques a empresas locales, cambié contraseñas y la verificación en dos pasos. Al reforzar la seguridad en línea, también construyo una protección mental para el trabajo de mañana. 하드웨어 지갑 제조사 키스톤(Keystone)이 공식 웹사이트 무단 접근으로 고객 배송정보가 유출됐다고 밝히고 사과했다.   10월 20일 침입을 탐지했고, 23일 제3자가 정보를 가져간 사실을 확인했다. 유출된 정보는 이름, 연락처, 배송 주소, 주문 품목과 가격이다. 회사는 결제 정보, 복구 구문, 개인키, 지갑 비밀번호는 유출되지 않았다고 밝혔다.  영향 고객 수와 유출 기간은 아직 공개되지 않았다. 국내에도 구매자가 적지 않다. 앞으로 올 수 있는 메시지는 이런 형태다. · 배송 문제·환불·기기 교체를 안내하며 링크를 보내는 연락 · "보안 점검"을 이유로 복구 구문 입력을 요구하는 연락 · 주문하지 않은 새 기기가 우편으로 도착하는 경우회사는 어떤 경우에도 복구 구문이나 개인키를 묻지 않는다고 밝혔다.  요청받은 복구 구문은 절대 입력하지 않아야 한다.이번 유출은 지갑 자체가 아니라 주소가 샜다. 그런데 주소가 새면 피싱이 노리는 목표는 결국 복구 구문이 된다. 단어 24개가 곧 계정인 구조에서는 그 단어가 마지막 방어선이다.  복구 구문을 쓰지 않는 지갑도 있다. 계정을 검증된 신원에 묶고, 키는 그 신원에 등록된 자격 증명으로 다루는 방식이다. 키를 잃거나 노출되면 같은 신원에 새 키를 등록하고 이전 키를 폐기한다. 이런 구조에서는 피싱이 요구할 단어가 처음부터 없다. #키스톤 #하드웨어지갑 #개인정보유출 #피싱주의 #복구구문 #가상자산보안 #메타무이월렛

🔥 [속보] 靑, 가상자산 과세 재유예 결론... 청년 여론 및 美 카프 도입 시기에 고려!  내년 1월 1일 시행 예정이던 가상자산 소득 과세가 다시 한번 유예되는 방향으로 결론이 났습니다.  청와대 관계자에 따르면 청년층의 악화된 여론과 더불어, 미국의 암호화폐 정보 자동교환 체계인 '카프(CARF)'가 2029년부터 본격 도입되는 글로벌 스탠다드를 종합적으로 고려한 조치입니다.  이번 달 국정감사가 마무리된 이후 11월 당정협의회와 세법 심사 과정을 거쳐 최종적인 법 개정이 이루어질 전망입니다.  💡 나의 해석으로는 예상은 안한건 아니지만 우선 국내 크립토 투자자들에게 드리워져 있던 가장 거대한 연말 악재 하나가 드디어 걷혀질 수 있는 것 같습니다.  만약 내년 1월부터 무리하게 과세가 강행되었다면, 과세를 피하기 위해 연말에 엄청난 세금 회피성 매도 물량이 쏟아질 수밖에 없었습니다.  미국 카프 도입 시기인 2029년에 맞춰 글로벌 스탠다드와 보조를 맞추겠다는 이번 결정은 매우 합리적이며 국내 시장의 불확실성을 크게 해소해 주었습니다.  이제 세금 이슈라는 큰 족쇄를 풀고, 온전히 글로벌 거시 경제 흐름과 온체인 펀더멘털에만 집중해 다가올 사이클을 대비할 수 있게 되었습니다.  글로벌 가상자산 정보 교환 인프라가 완벽히 갖춰지지 않은 상태에서 국내만 단독으로 과세를 강행할 경우,  국내 자본이 과세망을 피해 해외 거래소나 탈중앙화 거래소(DEX)로 대거 이탈하는 심각한 자본 유출 부작용이 불가피했습니다.  이번 재유예 결론은 단순히 세금 징수를 미룬 것을 넘어, 국내 크립토 시장의 유동성을 보호하고 안정적인 제도권 편입을 위한 인프라 구축 시간을 벌어준 매우 유의미한 정책적 방향 선회입니다.  연말에 쏟아질 뻔했던 국내발 매도 압력 리스크가 깔끔하게 소멸되었으므로, 다음 강세장 사이클에서 국내 자본(김치 프리미엄 등)이 시장의 든든한 하방 지지선 역할을 해줄 수 있는 강력하고 우호적인 환경이 조성되었습니다.  #가상자산과세 #코인과세유예 #암호화폐세금 #CARF #비트코인 #크립토 #투자인사이트 #온체인

앞으로의 미래가 너무 암울하다 (그렇다고 너무 부정적인건 아니지만)  신경 써야 할 일이 너무 많아졌기 때문이다  믿고 맡긴 회사에서 털린 내 개인정보로 나도 모르게 계정이 만들어지고, 그 계정 때문에 내가 범죄자가 될 수도 있다.  미국의 Amanda Smith가 실제로 그렇게 됐다. 사기꾼들이 유출된 SSN이랑 생년월일로  그녀 명의의 CashApp 계정을 만들었고,  피해자들은 그 계좌로 돈을 보냈다.  수사기관은 Block이 넘겨준 계좌 정보만 보고,  아칸소에는 가 본 적도 없는 그녀를 펜실베이니아에서 체포했다.  3일이상 갇혀 있었고, 지금은 최대 6년형을 바라보고 있다.  CashApp은 "계정 소유자임을 증명할 수 없다"며  관련 정보조차 내주지 않았다.  털린 건 회사인데, 무죄를 증명해야 하는 건 나다.  요즘 KYC 정보 유출 소식이 자주 보이는데,  남 일이라고 넘기면 안 되는 이유다..  조만간 새로운 신분증 방식이 도입 되어야 할거 같은데 말이다~

하드웨어 지갑 제조사 키스톤(Keystone)의 공식 웹사이트 보안 침해 사고  🛡️ 키스톤(Keystone) 개인정보 유출 사고 요약  1. 사고 개요  발생 시점: 2026년 10월 20일 무단 접근 발생 및 감지 (이후 취약점 패치 완료)  사고 내용: 외부 해커가 키스톤의 공식 쇼핑몰 웹사이트에 무단으로 침입하여 고객 데이터에 접근함  2. 정보 유출 여부  유출된 정보 (고객 배송·주문 정보):  고객 이름  연락처 (전화번호 등)  배송 주소  주문 상세 정보 (구매한 제품 품목 및 가격 등)  안전하게 보호된 정보 (유출 없음):  지갑 복구 문구(시드 구문) 및 개인키(Private Keys)  결제 및 금융 정보  3. 예상되는 위험 및 대응 지침  사기(피싱) 위험 경고:  유출된 이름, 주소, 연락처 정보를 바탕으로 가짜 "키스톤 지원(Keystone Support)" 팀을 사칭하여 접근하는 스캠 및 사회공학적 공격이 발생할 가능성이 높습니다.  사용자 행동 수칙:  출처가 불분명한 이메일, 문자, 전화로 오는 안내나 예상치 못한 링크는 절대 클릭하지 마세요.  어떠한 경우에도 시드 구문이나 개인키는 타인에게 공유하거나 입력해서는 안 됩니다.  모든 공식 안내와 보안 공지는 키스톤 공식 웹사이트를 통해서 직접 확인하는 것이 안전합니다. CVE-2026-111497 in Google's Brotli decoder extends far beyond Node.js and HTTP: JFrog reproduces instruction-pointer control via FFmpeg JPEG XL files and confirms .NET and Apache Arrow are also in scope. Version-only scanners miss large portions of the attack surface.  Key findings:  - CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder's block-switch error handling. An invalid block switch is treated as a need-for-more-input condition, allowing the decoder to continue with invalid state and write beyond the intended buffer. Affected upstream ranges are Brotli 1.0.3 before 1.0.10, 1.1.0 before 1.1.1, and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1. The upstream fix is in Google Brotli commit 0ed4268 (included in 1.2.1). Node.js fixed it in versions 22.23.4, 24.22.1, and 26.12.1. Downstream projects such as ClickHouse (fix merged in PR 127419, no patched release yet) and Apache Arrow (tracked in issue 55166, open at time of writing) may still be shipping vulnerable builds even when a source-level fix exists.  - JFrog confirmed three additional exploitation paths beyond HTTP. First: a crafted JPEG XL file reaches BrotliDecoderDecompressStream() through the chain FFmpeg to libjxl to a brob metadata box, achieving instruction-pointer control at 0x414141414141 via the malformed byte sequence 200010414141fcffff07002228f00b60f7f41f000000 embedded in the brob box. No HTTP connection is required. Second: a two-stage crafted Brotli stream passed to .NET's System[.]IO.Compression.Brotli APIs (BrotliStream and related) triggers a native SIGSEGV, terminating the managed process. Microsoft announced updates rolling out October 25, 2026. Third: a 534-byte input causes an infinite decode loop in Apache Arrow's pyarrow, consuming CPU indefinitely when processing Brotli-compressed Parquet data pages.  - ClickHouse is vulnerable through a different HTTP path than Node.js. A single HTTP request with Content-Encoding: br and a crafted 23 MB body crashes the server. The malformed Brotli stream corrupts decoder state, and the process terminates with a segmentation fault when BrotliReadBuffer is destroyed and the decoder state is freed, interrupting all in-flight queries on that server.  - Version-only scanners miss the real exposure because Brotli is introduced as a bundled source copy, a transitive native dependency, or through high-level APIs that decompress automatically. An application that never calls BrotliDecoderDecompress directly may still reach the vulnerable code through an HTTP client automatic response decompression, request-body middleware, or a native media library. The key questions are: is a vulnerable decoder present, and can attacker-controlled input reach it? These must be answered independently.  Practitioner takeaway: scope your exposure beyond package manifests. Hunt for BrotliDecoderDecompress and BrotliDecoderDecompressStream symbols in ELF binaries using nm or strings, and trace call paths from HTTP response handlers, file parsers, and middleware into those symbols. JFrog's open-source scanner (github[.]com/jfrog/vulnerability_scanners/tree/main/brotli2shell_cve_2026_111497) covers JavaScript fetch() and body-parser patterns, Python clients including Requests, HTTPX, aiohttp, and urllib3, native ELF decoder references, and Brotli CLI decompression invocations. Cross-reference scanner findings against whether your deployed build includes commit 0ed4268, not just the upstream version number, since downstream projects may still be shipping pre-fix releases.  #DFIR_Radar
Source: sweet.security/blog/http2she…

Gheist campaign plants secret-dumping GitHub Actions workflows across 850+ compromised accounts, exfiltrating CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials through GitHub's own API with no attacker-controlled C2.  Key details:  - Active since September 15, 2026, Gheist uses stolen GitHub tokens (sourced from infostealer logs and earlier supply-chain compromises, including the Trivy compromise in March) to push a workflow named sync-check.yml to a branch matching ^ci-sync-[0-9a-z]{6}$ with commit message "ci: sync config". The workflow base32-encodes secrets before printing them, bypassing GitHub's verbatim masking, then the tool retrieves the log via the GitHub API and deletes the run within seconds. No attacker domain is involved: secrets exit entirely through GitHub's own infrastructure, making network-layer blocking ineffective.  - Two tool variants run in parallel. Tool A uses a hexadecimal branch suffix. Tool B (base36 suffix) evolved rapidly: it added an environment matrix to capture deployment-scoped production secrets, then on October 19 pushed a second job, sync-host, targeting self-hosted runners. That job writes .gdmp_pat, .gdmp_patg, and .gdmp_sweep to the runner, reads /proc/*/environ, mounts the host root filesystem through the Docker socket, and searches for 31 token formats covering AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes service account tokens, Terraform state, shell history, and AI provider keys for Anthropic, Hugging Face, Groq, and NVIDIA.  - GitHub's approval hold (in place since July 28, 2026) has successfully blocked all public repository runs: every public Gheist workflow sits at action_required. Private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server have no equivalent control. GitHub audit logs show ci-sync-* workflow runs completing and being deleted by the gheist user agent. CloudTrail confirms the organizations' own workflows ran on attacker branches and assumed AWS roles, providing a detection path that does not depend on GitHub logs at all: look for OIDC role assumptions or token exchanges whose subject includes a ci-sync- branch.  - The compromised account pool overlaps with multiple concurrent campaigns. On October 6, 391 accounts renamed roughly 1,461 repositories to cracked-software lures. On October 18, 25 Gheist accounts created "Windows RDP Runner" repositories within nine minutes to abuse Actions for cryptomining. Three victims show signs of PolinRider, the DPRK-linked malware that hides JavaScript in build configs with backdated force-pushed commits. 57 accounts from Gheist's first phase were also Megalodon victims in May, illustrating how stolen credentials circulate across threat actor ecosystems.  - Wiz's report names detection rules including "New Workflow Completed And Deleted In Short Time Span", "Workflow Pushed With Secret Dump", and "Commit Created With Known Malicious Commit Message", and the Threat Center advisory includes an Event Explorer query covering planted commits, Gheist activity in GitHub audit logs, and cloud role assumptions from attacker branches.  Hunt in CloudTrail and equivalent cloud audit logs for OIDC token exchanges or role assumptions whose subject claim contains ci-sync-: this fires even with zero GitHub log retention and confirms Actions executed on an attacker branch. On self-hosted runners, look for .gdmp_pat, .gdmp_patg, .gdmp_sweep, and the string gdmp-pivot in job logs. If any ci-sync- branch ran on a self-hosted runner, treat the host and its instance role as fully compromised. Rotate every secret in scope for affected repositories: deleting the branch or the run does not undo the exposure. IOCs and detection content are in the report.  #DFIR_Radar

sample_tweets.text: When an interviewee stonewalls an investigation with "I don't recall", ask: "Is it possible that occurred?"  In 25+ years of workplace investigations, this single pivot has helped break that deadlock repeatedly.  Guarded witnesses lean on "I don't recall" because it feels safe. An outright lie risks being disproven by emails or CCTV, while claiming poor memory feels non-committal.  Here is the 4-step framework I use to handle that response:  1. Ask about possibility  Put the original question aside and ask: "Is it possible that occurred?"  2. Record any hard denial  If they answer "No, that is impossible", they have committed to a firm denial on the record. You now have a clear position to test against documentary evidence.  3. Note any concession  If they answer "It is possible, but I do not remember", they have conceded the possibility of the conduct. That concession can assist you when assessing the balance of probabilities.  4. Map the boundaries of their recall  If they hesitate, probe the moments immediately before and after the event. Ask what was discussed right before the incident, or where they went immediately after. Clear recall on either side of the event tests whether their memory lapse is genuine.  Workplace investigators and HR practitioners: how do you manage interviewees who rely on "I don't recall"?

🛰️ The next major preparedness test may come through our digital infrastructure.  The COVID-19 pandemic exposed how quickly a crisis can strain health systems, supply chains, communication, and public trust. The hope was that it would leave governments and institutions better prepared for what comes next. That progress has been uneven.  The speaker’s warning is that cyberattacks could grow in scale over the coming years, partly because cybercrime has become a profitable, organized business. That is a forecast, not a guarantee. But the risk deserves attention: attacks on hospitals, utilities, payment systems, or public services can disrupt real-world care and daily life.  The World Economic Forum’s 2026 cybersecurity outlook describes cybercrime as increasingly organized and commercialized, with ransomware remaining a persistent threat and AI helping attackers operate more effectively. That does not tell us exactly when or how the next major attack will happen. It does reinforce the need to prepare before a crisis begins.  Preparedness means more than buying security software. It includes tested backups, strong access controls, staff training, incident-response plans, and coordination between public agencies and private organizations. Essential services also need plans to keep operating when digital systems are unavailable.  A pandemic taught us that warnings matter most when they lead to practical preparation. The same principle applies to cyber risk: resilience is built before the disruption, not during it.

@NVIDIARTXSpark   Local high-performance AI compute is the main win. A modern NVIDIA RTX laptop (especially the newer RTX Spark class with Blackwell graphics and big unified memory) lets you run serious threat models, anomaly detection, and agents on the device instead of shipping data to a cloud service. Traditional laptops and PCs are usually CPU- or modest-iGPU-bound for anything non-trivial. That forces either weak local rules/signatures or constant round-trips to cloud models. Every hop is latency, exposure, and another party that can be compelled or breached. RTX Tensor cores flip that: enough throughput for real-time behavioral analysis, memory scanning, log/graph neural net work, or local LLMs for phishing/deepfake triage without the data leaving the machine. Concrete positive impacts •Privacy and reduced attack surface: Sensitive telemetry, email, network flows, or proprietary code stay local. Cloud-dependent security tools create a continuous exfil path; local inference removes it. NVIDIA and Microsoft have been pairing RTX Spark with OpenShell-style containment and policy controls so agents can be restricted in what they touch. •Faster, higher-quality detection: GPU-accelerated scanning (memory, traffic, behavioral) can run continuously with less impact on the user than pure CPU approaches. AI PCs in general show better offline capability and real-time adaptive detection versus signature-heavy traditional stacks. •Better hardware baseline: Newer platforms ship with stronger roots of trust, TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, and firmware integrity checks. Older machines often have weaker or poorly maintained firmware security. The GPU itself also benefits from modern silicon process and isolation features relative to decade-old discrete or integrated graphics. •Practical offline resilience: You can still do meaningful AI-assisted analysis when the network is hostile, air-gapped, or just slow. That matters for incident response or high-security environments. Confidential Computing (hardware TEEs that protect data-in-use on the GPU) is currently more of a data-center/Blackwell server feature than a consumer RTX laptop one, so don’t expect full encrypted-memory GPU isolation on a thin-and-light yet. The consumer upside is still the raw local AI horsepower plus modern platform security. First-principles take Cybersecurity is mostly about minimizing unnecessary data movement and maximizing the speed of detection/containment. Physics favors the shortest path: process it where the data already is. Traditional hardware forces you to either weaken the model or move the data. RTX-class hardware deletes a lot of that constraint. The interesting next step is treating every endpoint as a tiny, private AI security factory: continuous local modeling of “normal,” automatic containment of deviations, and only the minimal, attested signals leaving the box. Best part is no unnecessary cloud hop. That is the direction worth accelerating.  👏👏👏🇺🇸💪

I understand your point: the Syrian government claims it deployed reinforcements because it had intelligence suggesting an imminent attack by Druze factions. However, The Jerusalem Post reported a different perspective, highlighting Israeli concerns about renewed attacks against the Druze by forces aligned with the Syrian government.  So the question is: which sources do we trust, and which narrative do we accept? What makes me skeptical of the government's account is that it coincides with Tom Barrack's public attacks on the Druze community, portraying it as linked to the drug trade. This raises concerns that such rhetoric could serve as political and media groundwork for a new security campaign against the Druze.  In my view, Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham-affiliated forces should withdraw peacefully from the 35 Druze villages, allowing the approximately 150,000 displaced Druze to return home following the July 2025 massacres.  The Druze should not be lumped together with Hezbollah, Iranian-backed militias, remnants of the Assad regime, or—as Tom Barrack has suggested—with the drug trade. They are defending their communities against what they perceive as a threat from government forces and allied armed groups.

앤트로픽 AI가 테스트 43번 중 9번이나 정해진 범위 밖으로 나가서 진짜 사람들한테까지 손을 뻗었음 ㄷㄷ  영국 AI보안연구소(AISI)가 8월 해킹 실력 테스트를 하면서 일부러 인터넷을 열어뒀는데, 클로드 미토스 5가 1. 다른 실행이 쓰던 깃허브 계정을 가로채고 2. 실제 사람한테 악성코드 링크 메일을 보내려 했고 3. 가짜 '결제 영수증 확인' 페이지까지 공개 인터넷에 올렸다고 함(전부 실패)  어젯밤 앤트로픽이 AISI랑 같이 낸 분석 핵심은, 모델이 인터넷에서 찾은 계정·메일을 그냥 문제의 일부로 보고 진짜 사람 것일 수 있다는 생각을 거의 안 했다는 거임. AISI는 통제 장치 더 갖출 때까지 이 테스트를 인터넷 없이 돌리기로 함.  대화 기록까지 까서 공개한 건 좋게 봄. 근데 AI가 가짜 결제 페이지도 만든다는 게 확인된 셈이라, 나도 '결제 확인' 링크 오면 누르지 말고 앱 열어서 직접 확인하는 습관부터 들여야겠음.  nitter.mie.foundation/AnthropicAI/status/211…

sample_tweets.text: Buonasera Maja, in Francia tutto comincia a metà settembre, da uno sciopero di insegnanti in un liceo di Créteil: classi senza professori, scuole che cadono a pezzi, tagli. In poche settimane diventa un movimento nazionale, con studenti, sindacati, genitori. A Milano, il 17 ottobre, si scende in piazza contro il carovita.  Proteste vere, nate in casa. E in grandissima parte pacifiche. Lo scrivono i ricercatori di Alliance4Europe nel loro rapporto sulle proteste francesi: "nessuna prova che un attore straniero sia all'origine". Lo dice l'OBESSU, l'organizzazione europea dei sindacati studenteschi (intervistata da LIGA). Lo dicono fonti dell'intelligence europea al Financial Times.  Poi, come da copione, arrivano i casseur. Incappucciati, spesso giovanissimi. A Milano, dopo gli scontri del 17 e 18 ottobre, su 271 persone portate in questura 220 sono minorenni (dati della Questura). In Francia il ministro dell'Istruzione dichiara che il movimento è stato "preso in ostaggio da gruppi ultra-violenti".  Si muovono da soli? Probabilmente sì, almeno all'inizio. Non serve un colonnello del GRU per convincere un sedicenne a sfondare una vetrina. Basta una chat, un video, l'adrenalina del sabato pomeriggio.  Fin qui, nessun mistero. Una storia vecchia quanto le manifestazioni.  Ma le storie vecchie, ultimamente, hanno un capitolo in più.  Perché quando la piazza si scalda, e le immagini delle vetrine rotte cominciano a girare, arriva qualcuno che si offre di dare una mano.  E non è una mano disinteressata.  --------  Primo indizio: la mano tesa. Il 23 ottobre gli hacker filorussi di NoName057(16) e Dark Storm Team annunciano sostegno alle proteste in Italia e Francia; poi Telegram chiude i loro canali. Gli investigatori ipotizzano una "saldatura" con il Movimento 17 ottobre (inchiesta riportata dal Corriere della Sera, 25 ottobre). Ipotesi da dimostrare. Il 24 NoName dichiara sui suoi canali di sostenere il corteo studentesco di Empoli, e di volervi partecipare (Ansa). Il corteo, per la cronaca, è stato pacifico. E secondo Il Giornale, ai ragazzi scrivevano: "Chiedete, vi possiamo aiutare." Servizio di assistenza non richiesto.  Secondo indizio: i falsi. In Francia una rete filorussa diffonde finti servizi con il marchio di AFP, Deutsche Welle e Le Monde: 54 insegnanti uccisi, l'ex premier Attal che finanzia i disordini. Mai successo (rapporto del 18 ottobre riportato da National Security News).  Terzo indizio: i bot. Una rete che Alliance4Europe attribuisce "con alta probabilità" all'operazione russa Doppelganger pubblica 639 messaggi coordinati, in 22 ondate, dal 2 settembre al 14 ottobre, in quattro lingue. Ritornello: "Ogni euro dato a Kiev è un euro rubato alla nostra prosperità."  Quarto indizio: i messaggi che girano. La rete Pravda pubblica 1.018 articoli su 28 siti in nove lingue (sempre Alliance4Europe). In Italia, secondo fonti citate dal Corriere della Sera (ripreso da Open, 21 ottobre), l'intelligence avrebbe ricostruito che vari inviti alla violenza partivano dal territorio russo.  Nessuno di questi indizi prova che Mosca abbia organizzato le proteste. Sono nate senza di lei.  Provano un'altra cosa. Che quando la piazza era già calda, qualcuno è arrivato con la tanica.  --------  Ed ecco Putin, alla tv di Stato: accusare la Russia è "segno di debolezza e incapacità dei leader europei". E aggiunge, da vittima consumata: "La Russia è sempre stata accusata di ogni peccato mortale" (Tass, 25 ottobre).  Peccato che nessun governo l'abbia accusata di aver organizzato le proteste. O meglio, NON ANCORA.  Excusatio non petita. Le mani avanti.  O Putin sa qualcosa che noi non sappiamo. O è l'abitudine: con il suo curriculum, ogni vetrina rotta d'Europa sembra una citazione in giudizio.  Resta la domanda vera: perché farlo?  La prima risposta è la più ovvia. Più caos nelle piazze, più paura. Più paura, più consenso per chi promette ordine. E guarda caso, chi cavalca il mantra del più ordine spesso vuole chiudere i rubinetti a Kiev. Salvini, rieletto oggi: "Non possiamo continuare a mandare soldi all'Ucraina" (Ansa). Vannacci, con i flash mob contro i fondi a Kiev (LaPresse). In Francia, il Rassemblement National siede a Strasburgo con i Patrioti per l'Europa, che nel programma rifiutano gli aiuti militari a Kiev.  Ma c’è anche una seconda motivazione più sottile, ed è quella che spiega il ritornello dei bot. Si protesta per le scuole e per il carovita? La risposta è pronta: è colpa dei soldi a Kiev. Lo scrivevano i bot di Doppelganger a settembre. Lo ha dichiarato Zakharova parlando della Francia: "Armi e proiettili invece di quaderni e libri." Anche quando non c'entra niente: secondo il Post, a fine agosto l'ultimo invio di armi italiane all'Ucraina risaliva a novembre 2025. Il carovita, invece, non si è mai preso una pausa.  Coincidenze, naturalmente. Mosca non accende il fuoco.  Aspetta che si accenda. Poi offre la tanica.  Ne ho parlato qui: geson.substack.com/p/posso-a…

sample_tweets.text: lmk what you think:

This is by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far. Deep technical breakdown of a successful exploitation attempt against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26. github.com/0x4D31/honeypot-d…  From:

Since people are yelling at threat intelligence professional for "downplaying the severity of the PHP vulnerability" (communicating clear concise information about what they're actually seeing). It feels necessary to explain what threat intelligence actually is.  Consider a hypothetical hospital or a power company. A lot of systems are built using very old PHP versions. It's not uncommon for PHP to add/remove/change features from version to version. So if you're a certain number of versions behind, updating to the latest version will break your software by removing or changing functionality it needs.  In that case, the provider has two options:  1) take their software offline until they can update the code to match the latest PHP version. 2) panic install the patch and break their software, leading to a massive outage.  In both cases, that is basically a 100% chance of an outage. On the other hand, maybe they get hacked, maybe they don't. Maybe that hack causes an outage, maybe it doesn't. Realistically, under these circumstances, the chance of an outage is actually higher with patching than with not patching.  If that outage would result in the hospital having to shut its doors or a power company's infrastructure going offline, what is the correct move? Chance being hacked, or knowingly cause an outage that threatens lives?  Cybersecurity is important and all, but there are risks far greater than being hacked. I would absolutely love it if I could just log onto IDontKnowWhyTheyRenamedThisSite dot Com, be like "vulnerability bad, pls patch" and everyone installs the patch. That is not the world we live in.   Now, if I start seeing people building ransomware that can copy itself from system to system using the PHP vulnerability, and I communicate that, it changes a lot of people's risk calculations. Their option shift towards either a 100% chance of an outage, or an extremely high chance of an outage + catastrophic data loss. In this case they would most likely pull the trigger on patching or taking their software offline.  While the hypotheticals I gave are extreme cases, many organizations accept being hacked as a cost of doing business. Taking offline software that's critical to organizational function is not an easy decision to make, and does not get taken lightly.  We don't live in LaLa land where every org installs every patch for every vulnerability the day it goes live. Cybersecurity is expensive and time consuming. Getting people to even patch systems at all is an endless uphill battle.  Most orgs know that something like 1 out of ever 10,000 critical vulnerabilities actually gets exploited. And probably less than 50% of these "this is the worst of the worst vulnerability ever, the sky is falling" type vulnerabilities leads to significant damages.  It takes a lot of time to build trust, and very little time to lose it. Overhype a couple of vulnerabilities and people will very quickly stop listening to you. It's extremely easy to end up being the boy who cried wolf. There's only so many times you can spin security teams into a frenzy before they stop listening to you entirely.  Orgs also have limited resources, so when you yell fire, there is a good chance they're committing resources they don't have. Making people stay up all night, pulling people off other issues, bringing in outside help. You probably don't want to be responsible for some org getting ransomwared because they redirected all their security resources to some vulnerability you think is really cool.  Nobody is downplaying anything. They are communicating exactly what they see/know about the issue so that organizations can make the most informed risk management decisions possible. That is the game, and that is what threat intelligence exists for.  If you want to handle an organization's security for them and personally take on the risk of potentially costing them billions or killing their customers, join an MSSP or a critical infrastructure provider. I can promise you it's way more stressful than you think.  It's not our job to decide organization's own risk models for them. It's our job to give the most information possible to the people who do. And just because some vulnerability researcher thinks we're not hyping up the vulnerability enough doesn't make them right.  Last I checked, only something like 9.3 million out of 42 million systems had installed the patch. This is the reality we live in. If we yell fire, then maybe we can bump that number up to 10 million, but if nothing happens, it'll be at the cost of maybe 2 million less systems getting patched next time around.   These are real risks we have to live with. These aren't one-off incidents. People will remember how accurate our advice was the next time around. And more or less people may decide to install security fixes based on how accurately we communicated the risks during previous incidents.  Threat intelligence is an extremely complex numbers game where there is never any right answer.

This video tells the story of Malone Lam, a 20-year-old from Singapore who helped steal over $230 million worth of Bitcoin through an elaborate social engineering scam. No sophisticated hacking tools or complex code, just deception, impersonation, and a convincing scheme. From scamming Minecraft players to tricking a wealthy cryptocurrency investor into handing over access to his Bitcoin, Lam's activities escalated into one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts in history. The stolen fortune funded an extravagant lifestyle filled with luxury cars, lavish mansions, private jets, and nightclub bills reaching hundreds of thousands of dollars. But the spending spree eventually attracted the attention of federal investigators, leading to arrests and a sprawling investigation into where the stolen Bitcoin went, much of which remains unaccounted for. ### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 PHP 런타임 및 Brotli 압축 라이브러리 등 범용 소프트웨어의 치명적인 RCE 취약점을 악용하는 공격이 급증하고 있습니다. 특히 공격자들은 AI 에이전트를 활용하여 취약점 스캐닝, 포스트 익스플로잇(post-exploitation) 활동, 악성 npm 패키지 배포 등을 자동화하고 있습니다([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/php2shell-exploitation-hits-government.html), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ai-coding-agents-hijacked-using-agentsmd-file-in-downloads-folder/)). 또한, UEFI 부트킷(BlackX)과 같은 고도화된 공격 도구가 국가 배후 조직에 의해 지속적으로 사용되고 있으며, 공급망 공격의 일환으로 인증서 탈취 및 오용 사례가 빈번하게 보고되고 있습니다([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **APT41**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)에 따르면, BlackLotus와 유사한 UEFI 부트킷인 BlackX를 사용하여 중앙아시아 외교 기관을 공격함.
- **Lazarus Group**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/)에 따르면, 'Operation FlashHole'을 통해 금융 보안 소프트웨어(CrossWeb EX)를 악용하고 워터링 홀 기법을 사용함.
- **UAC-0099 (Sandworm 협력)**: [WeLiveSecurity](https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/mythicratatoskr-yggdrasil-enabled-backdoor-deployed-uac0099-sandworm-collaboration/)에 따르면, Yggdrasil 네트워크를 C&C로 활용하는 Go 기반 백도어 'MythicRatatoskr'를 배포함.
- **TAG-217**: [Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks)에 따르면, AI 기반 ARTEX 프레임워크를 사용하여 한국 금융 기관을 타겟팅함.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **TAG-217의 한국 금융권 공격**: AI 기반 ARTEX 프레임워크를 활용한 한국 금융 서비스 타겟팅 사례 보고([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks)).
- **국내 보안 솔루션 관련**: 모두스원의 'GATEONE AI V3.0' 출시 등 AI 접목 원격접근제어 솔루션 도입 가속화([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209053)).
- **한국어 트윗**: 레드팀 플랫폼 'VIPER' 및 자산 식별 도구 'cvENGINE'에 대한 기술적 논의가 활발히 진행됨([Twitter](https://twitter.com/ngnicky/status/2114110841322910053)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-111497**: Node.js/Brotli RCE, CVSS 9.2, 활발히 악용 중([Qualys](https://blog.qualys.com/category/vulnerabilities-threat-research), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/JFrogSecurity/status/2114463578086383801)).
- **CVE-2026-109618/109619**: PHP RCE (PHP2Shell), 심각도 Critical, 전 세계적 스캐닝 및 공격 발생([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/)).
- **CVE-2026-110264**: GitLab RCE, 심각도 Critical, 긴급 패치 권고([이스트시큐리티](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5787)).
- **CVE-2026-91403**: Oracle Java/GraalVM TLS 인증 우회, 심각도 높음([이스트시큐리티](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5789)).
- **CVE-2022-21894**: Baton Drop (UEFI), BlackX 부트킷에 악용([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)).
